biography.plain_text: Peter Burnet is a British chartered designer whose portfolio includes seagoing and riverside projects. His FCSD designation marks senior professional recognition. His work includes the combined exterior and interior conception of Spirit of the East. He also devised Spirit of Chelsea, a 23-metre floating venue for hospitality and events on the River Thames.

long_biography.plain_text:
Burnet conceived Spirit of the East as a steel sailing vessel for extended travel, taking responsibility for its outward form and onboard spaces. He engaged a specialist naval architecture firm to convert the concept into the calculations and technical plans required for construction. The Turkish builder completed the project in 2006, providing a rare example of an owner-originated idea developed through specialist naval collaboration.

Spirit of Chelsea shifted both scale and setting. Planned as a houseboat for London event charters, it placed accommodation and entertainment functions within a fixed urban mooring rather than a long-range sailing platform. The contrast reveals Burnet’s interest in arranging marine interiors around how people gather and move, while his use of specialist partners shows a concept-led approach grounded in practical delivery.
